Empirical Research Plan – “History-Dependent Loan Pricing”

--------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy  

Method: Two–Stage Least Squares (Instrumental-Variables panel regression).

Rationale  
• The main endogenous regressor is the borrower’s previous loan spread (Spread_last).  
• Spread_last is correlated with unobserved, persistent borrower risk (ε) that also affects today’s spread (Spread_curr).  
• Quarter-to-quarter fluctuations in the aggregate loan market spread (AggSpread_q) at the time of the borrower’s last loan are powerful predictors of Spread_last but are plausibly exogenous to ε once we control for (i) current credit-cycle conditions, (ii) borrower fundamentals, and (iii) firm fixed effects.  
• Thus AggSpread_q (and close variants) are valid instruments: they generate quasi-random variation in Spread_last that comes only from macro credit-supply shocks and not from the borrower’s own risk.

Mathematically  

First stage Spread_last_it  = π·AggSpread_q(i,t-1)  + X_it-1β + φ_i + τ_t + u_it  
Second stage Spread_curr_it = γ·Ŝpread_last_it + X_itβ + φ_i + τ_t + ε_it  

where φ_i are firm fixed effects (FE) and τ_t are calendar-quarter FE.

--------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control

Treatment variable (continuous): Spread_last_it ≡ all-in-drawn spread (in bps over LIBOR) on the firm’s most recent previous syndicated loan.  

Instrument (Z): AggSpread_q(i,t-1) = average all-in-drawn spread for all U.S. syndicated term loans and revolvers originated in the same calendar quarter q as the borrower’s last loan.

Interpretation in binary language (for intuition only)  
• “Treated” observations = borrowers whose last loan occurred in a “tight” credit quarter (AggSpread in top tercile).  
• “Control” = borrowers whose last loan occurred in a “loose” quarter (bottom tercile).  
But the econometrics will use the continuous Z.

Timing  
• Event date = signing date of the new loan (t).  
• Instrument date = signing quarter of the previous loan (t-1).  
No running variable / cutoff (not an RDD).

--------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions

A1. Instrument relevance: Aggregate spreads at date t-1 strongly predict the borrower’s own Spread_last.  
 • Highly plausible; market-wide conditions are the dominant determinant of contemporaneous loan pricing (testable via first-stage F-statistic).

A2. Exclusion restriction: Conditional on current fundamentals, current aggregate spreads, and firm FE, AggSpread_q(t-1) affects Spread_curr only through its effect on Spread_last.  
 • Plausible because the macro shock at t-1 is at least one year old. We partial out anything persistent via firm FE and anything current via τ_t and current controls.

A3. Independence / as-good-as-random: After conditioning, AggSpread_q(t-1) is orthogonal to the error term ε_it.  
 • Credible if borrowers did not time their last borrowing based on a forecast of their future private information; timing is often driven by investment needs and credit-cycle liquidity shocks.

A4. Monotonicity: A higher AggSpread_q(t-1) weakly increases every borrower’s Spread_last (no “defiers”).  
 • Reasonable in competitive loan market.

A5. Stable Unit Treatment Value (SUTVA): One firm’s exposure to a tight or loose past market does not directly affect another firm’s current spread after we control for current macro spreads.  
 • Plausible given syndication structure.

--------------------------------------------------------------
4. Main Threats and Mitigations

T1. Persistent borrower risk not fully captured by controls  
 • Mitigation: Include firm FE (absorbs time-invariant risk) and rich current fundamentals & ratings.  
 • Robustness: Interact controls with time-fixed effects; include firm-specific linear trends.

T2. Serial correlation of credit cycles (corr(Z, τ_t))  
 • Mitigation: Include calendar-quarter FE τ_t so that identification relies only on cross-sectional variation in the timing of firms’ previous borrowing, not on level differences across quarters.

T3. Selection/survival bias (only firms that come back are in the sample)  
 • Mitigation: Weight observations by inverse probability of re-borrowing estimated from logit selection model; show results unchanged.  Also test subsamples: healthy firms, unrated firms, constant lead-arranger relationships.

--------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline (executable)

```r
############################################################
# 0.  Libraries
############################################################
library(data.table)   # fast data wrangling
library(fixest)       # panel & IV regressions
library(lmtest); library(sandwich)  # robust SEs

############################################################
# 1.  Load data
############################################################
loans <- fread("dealscan_loans.csv")         # one row = loan tranche
comp  <- fread("compustat_quarterly.csv")    # borrower fundamentals

############################################################
# 2.  Merge and variable construction
############################################################
# Aggregate market spread by quarter
loans[ , quarter := as.yearqtr(SigningDate)]
agg_spread <- loans[ , .(AggSpread_q = mean(AllInDrawnSpread, na.rm = TRUE)),
                     by = quarter]

# Label each loan with previous loan info
setorder(loans, BorrowerID, SigningDate)
loans[ , Spread_last := shift(AllInDrawnSpread, 1, type = "lag"), by = BorrowerID]
loans[ , PrevDate    := shift(SigningDate,        1, type = "lag"), by = BorrowerID]
loans <- loans[!is.na(Spread_last)]   # keep only loans with a previous loan

# Instrument: Agg spread in quarter of previous loan
loans[ , PrevQuarter := as.yearqtr(PrevDate)]
loans <- merge(loans, agg_spread, by.x = "PrevQuarter", by.y = "quarter",
               all.x = TRUE, suffixes = c("", "_Instr"))

# Current quarter fixed effect
loans[ , CurrQuarter := as.yearqtr(SigningDate)]

# Merge Compustat (nearest previous fiscal quarter)
comp[ , CompQuarter := as.yearqtr(FiscalDate)]
loans <- merge(loans, comp, by.x = c("BorrowerID","CurrQuarter"),
               by.y = c("GVKEY","CompQuarter"), all.x = TRUE)

# Controls (example)
loans[ , `:=`(logAssets = log(Assets),
              Leverage  = TotalDebt / Assets,
              ROA       = EBIT / Assets,
              Rating_d  = factor(SandP_Rating))]

############################################################
# 3.  Main IV regression
############################################################
iv_formula <- AllInDrawnSpread ~ Spread_last + logAssets + Leverage + ROA + Rating_d |
                                  AggSpread_q + logAssets + Leverage + ROA + Rating_d

est_main <- feols(iv_formula,
                  data = loans,
                  fixef = ~ BorrowerID + CurrQuarter,
                  cluster = ~ BorrowerID)   # borrower-clustered SE

summary(est_main)

############################################################
# 4.  Robustness check – alternative instrument
#     Use Baa corporate bond spread in PrevQuarter (pre-computed)
############################################################
loans <- merge(loans, bond_spreads, by = "PrevQuarter", all.x = TRUE)
iv_alt <- update(iv_formula, . ~ . | BaaSpread_q + logAssets + Leverage + ROA + Rating_d)
est_alt <- feols(iv_alt, data = loans, fixef = ~ BorrowerID + CurrQuarter,
                 cluster = ~ BorrowerID)
etable(est_main, est_alt, tex = FALSE)
```

--------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results  

Economic intuition: If lenders (or borrowers) anchor on past deal terms, a 100-bp higher previous spread—caused solely by an exogenous tight market—should raise today’s spread even though current fundamentals warrant no premium. I expect:  

γ ≈ 0.20–0.30  
That is, 20–30 bps of the earlier 100-bp shock carry over into the new loan.

--------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (IV)

C1: Instrument relevance (F-stat > 10) ............................. 1  
C2: Exclusion restriction (no direct path) ........................ 0.5  
C3: Independence / no omitted serial shocks ....................... 0.5  
C4: Monotonicity (no defiers) ..................................... 1  
C5: SUTVA / no interference ....................................... 1  
TOTAL (out of 5) ................................................. 4.0  

Overall, the design is strong but hinges on the plausibility of the exclusion restriction and absence of long-lived unobserved shocks.
